angles.working_title: The biggest spender lost: who paid for Illinois' $55 million Senate primary
angles.interesting_fact: Raja Krishnamoorthi's campaign accounted for about $28.9 million of ad spending and Juliana Stratton's campaign about $1.1 million; she won, with a Pritzker-backed PAC adding $14.4 million for her and a crypto PAC $9.0 million against her.

Illinois Senate primary super PAC spending

financial_claims.claim: Senate primary ad spending and reservations $55.3M as of Mar 13; Krishnamoorthi $28.9M, Stratton $15.5M ($1.1M campaign, $14.4M Illinois Future PAC), Fairshake $9.0M against Stratton
financial_claims.attributed_to: AdImpact; includes reservations; not audited by LLF

angles.synopsis: AdImpact counted $55.3 million in Illinois Senate primary ad spending and reservations as of March 13, the most for a Senate primary in the state on record. Raja Krishnamoorthi's total, $28.9 million, came almost entirely from his campaign. Juliana Stratton's was $15.5 million, of which her campaign spent $1.1 million and the Pritzker-backed Illinois Future PAC $14.4 million; the crypto-focused PAC Fairshake spent $9.0 million attacking her, though outlets put its total between $5.5 million and nearly $10 million. Stratton won with 39.6 percent to Krishnamoorthi's 33.6 at 82 percent of precincts, per Capitol News Illinois, and faces Republican Don Tracy in November. No claim about what the money did is supported.

angles.working_title: Ford won with about 24 percent after a PAC spent nearly $5 million for the runner-up
angles.interesting_fact: FEC filings show the United Democracy Project, which AdImpact calls AIPAC-aligned, spent about $4.97 million supporting Melissa Conyears-Ervin; La Shawn Ford beat her with roughly 24 percent to 20.

angles.synopsis: In the Democratic primary for the open 7th District, La Shawn Ford finished first with about 24 percent in unofficial returns, ahead of Chicago Treasurer Melissa Conyears-Ervin at about 20. The United Democracy Project, described by AdImpact as an AIPAC-aligned PAC, supported Conyears-Ervin: LLF's de-duplicated count of its FEC independent expenditure filings is about $4.97 million, and AdImpact put it at $4.7 million as of March 13. The crypto PAC Fairshake spent about $1.9 million attacking Ford, per AdImpact. Retiring Rep. Danny Davis backed Ford, the Tribune reported. Ford faces Republican Chad Koppie Sr. in November.

angles.working_title: The congressman stepped aside at the last minute. His chief of staff was the only Democrat on the ballot
angles.interesting_fact: Rep. Jesus 'Chuy' Garcia filed to run, then withdrew; his chief of staff Patty Garcia filed just before the deadline and was the only Democrat in the primary; two independents were then removed from the ballot for falling short on signatures.

sources.headline: Two independents stricken from 4th District election ballot
Rep. Chuy Garcia discusses decision not to run for reelection

damaging_allegation.note: 'Coronation' and 'machine play' are critics' characterizations, attributed and answered by Garcia's stated reasons; no claim of coordination is made.

angles.synopsis: Rep. Jesus 'Chuy' Garcia filed petitions on Oct. 27, 2025, then withdrew; his chief of staff, Patty Garcia (no relation), filed shortly before the Nov. 3 deadline and was the only Democrat on the primary ballot. Garcia said his cardiologist advised him to step aside and his wife is fighting MS, and rejected the idea that he was anointing a successor; critics called the move a coronation. In July the State Board of Elections voted 8-0 to remove independents Byron Sigcho-Lopez and Mayra Macias, who needed 10,816 valid signatures to Garcia's 697; hearing officers found them 1,222 and 486 short. Sigcho-Lopez sued; no ruling has been found. The November ballot lists Patty Garcia (D), Lupe Castillo (R), Chris Getty (independent) and Ed Hershey (Working Class Party).

angles.working_title: Two AIPAC-backed winners are on the November ballot: Melissa Bean in IL-8 and Donna Miller in IL-2
angles.interesting_fact: Per AdImpact, Bean's $4.6 million included $4.2 million from three outside groups and Miller's $6.0 million included $4.4 million from Affordable Chicago Now; Common Dreams reports AIPAC-backed candidates won in both.

angles.working_title: AIPAC-linked spending targeted Biss first, then Abughazaleh. Biss won
angles.interesting_fact: Per Newsweek and Axios, Elect Chicago Women spent about $2.8 million for Laura Fine and $1.3 million against Daniel Biss; Chicago Progressive Partnership spent about $165,500 against Kat Abughazaleh; Biss won with 29.5 percent at 91 percent counted.
